title: Restoring a category brings its mapping back untouched
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location is connected to QuickBooks Online and that AccountingHub is not enabled.
  • Have a new No Charge category for this test, category A, mapped to an expense account and then archived.
custom_steps:
1. Open Administration > Service > Internal Work Orders.
  2. Click the "Show archived" link.
  3. Click Restore on category A.
  4. Open Integrations > QuickBooks.
  5. Open ShopView Accounts.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The categories page opens.

Step 2:

  • Category A is listed with Restore.

Step 3:

  • Category A is active again.

Step 4:

  • The QuickBooks page opens.

Step 5:

  • Category A's row is no longer greyed and shows the same account: nothing had to be mapped again.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11762 (Story 5, QuickBooks Online account mapping)

  • S5-R6: “The per-category mapping follows the per-row model of part categories, not the fixed ShopView Accounts keys: one row per category per location, keyed by the category's stable key. Archiving a category keeps its mapping; Restore brings it back untouched, nothing is mapped again. The rows exist from the release (S1-R13), so the accountant can map before the setting is on (S5-R5).”
